newsitem.title: GERMANY: INSTANT VIEW - German Feb Inudstrial Output.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - German Feb Inudstrial Output.

text.p: Following is a list of economists' reactions to German industrial output figures for February. The data showed a 1.9 percent month-on-month rise after a decline of 1.5 percent in January.

MATHIAS HAFFNER, economist at BZW in Frankfurt. "The numbers may have surprised the market a little bit, as they may have been slightly higher than the consensus estimate, but they likely reflect ongoing erratic movements in the construction sector and should not be interpreted as a shift to much stronger growth. On the other hand they signal some recovery, making it unlikely the Bundesbank will change rates today."

UWE ANGENENDT, economist at BHF Bank in Frankfurt. "The driving force behind the numbers appears to have come from the manufacturing sector which was already hinted at by the last Ifo report. Consequently there is reason for some optimisim as the numbers now present a slightly stronger picture for economic growth. We are therefore also slightly more optimistic for first quarter economic growth. But these numbers will not have any immediate impact on German interest rates. The recovery is still far too fragile and it will take quite a while for such a recovery to filter through and prompt a change in Bundesbank policies."

RALF KUGELSTADT, UBS: "The figures were stronger than expected, especially manufacturing performance. The market's focus should be on the performance in the manufacturing sector. These figures will fuel expectations that the economy will continue to recover."

Markets reacted poorly to the data with the Bund futures contract initially dipping 15 basis points after the news. The share market DAX index also gave up nearly half a percentage point, falling to 3,208.05 in pre-bourse trading. German February manufacturing orders are expected at 1000 GMT.
